Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

emotional adjective

moved, showing strong feeling

also get emotional, moved, in tears, an emotional moment

classical

Cic. Fam. 3.10.1: graviter prīmō nūntiō commōtus sum
Traupman 159: commōtus, upset

commōtus, commōta, commōtum

adjective: the participle of commoveō, often with the ablative of the cause

moved, stirred, upset

Latin says what moved the person and how much: graviter, vehementer commōtus. Without context it leans to agitation or distress (see affect).

Other words

  • permōtus, permōta, permōtum — deeply moved

    adjective: the participle of permoveō · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 10.4.6 (Lewis & Short): sīve īrācundiā, sīve dolōre, sīve metū permōtus

    Stronger than commōtus: thoroughly stirred, by anger, grief or fear; also “persuaded, induced” (Lewis & Short, s.v. permoveō).

  • lacrimās tenēre nōn posse — be unable to hold back one’s tears

    phrase · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.30.2: lacrimās nōn tenērēs

    Where English says “I got emotional”, Latin usually names the tears: sine lacrimīs, lacrimās tenēre.

Examples

  • ad tē vērō et ad nostram Tulliolam nōn queō sine plūrimīs lacrimīs scrībere

    but to you and our little Tullia I can’t write without many tearsCic. Fam. 14.2.1

  • haec tibi rīdicula videntur; nōn enim ades. quae sī vidērēs, lacrimās nōn tenērēs.

    these things seem funny to you, for you aren’t here. If you saw them, you couldn’t hold back your tears.Cic. Fam. 7.30.2

See also emotion, affect, cry.
